newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods steady to lower on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods steady to lower on weak demand.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot products prices were steady to lower late Thursday as refinery buying dried up and demand stayed sluggish following last week's flooding of northern California roads, traders said.
Interest in January shipments of gasoline thinned, with levels for San Francisco CARB grade holding at 74.50/75.50 cents gallon, unchanged from early, brokers said.
Bay area CARB got done at 76.50 cents a gallon, while prices for Los Angeles grades were steadily two cents higher.
Deals for February gasoline in San Francisco were done at 78.25, 78.50, and 77.75 cents a gallon, wholesale dealers said.
Traders said buying from refiners tailed off this week, cited Texaco and Mobil as two key buyers preparing for turnarounds later this month.
